units: <cite ref="Chullin 27a:4">Ḥull. 27ᵃ</cite> <he>ממקום ששָׁח וכ׳</he>, v. <cite ref="H00582"><he>חָטָא</he> I</cite>.

<cite ref="Chullin 27a:5">Ib.</cite> <he>שח … והוא שח ועומד הוא</he> ‘where it bends’ implies (that the limb which is to be cut) must be erect (when in its natural condition), but this (the tail) is always hanging down.

<cite ref="Jerusalem Talmud Taanit 2:2:4">Y. Taan. II, 65ᶜ</cite> top <he>צריך לָשׁוּחַ בכולן</he> (or <he>לָשׁוֹחַ</he> fr. <cite ref="U00634"><he>שחח</he></cite>) he must bend down with all of them (the eighteen vertebræ).
<cite ref="Pirkei Avot 5:21">Ab. V, 21</cite> <he>בן תשעים לָשׁוּחַ</he> at ninety years (is the time) for being bent (perh. meant as noun <he>לַשּׁוּחַ</he>).

<cite ref="Midrash Tehillim 48:2">Midr. Till. to Ps. XLVIII</cite> <he>לבו שח עליו</he> his heart within him is bent (in grief over his sin); <cite ref="Yalkut Shimoni on Nach 755">Yalk. ib. 755</cite> <he>סח</he> (corr. acc.); a. fr.
<cite ref="Midrash Tehillim 42:4">Midr. Till. to Ps. XLII</cite> <he>אני מתקנאה ומִשְׁתּוֹחַחַת וכ׳</he> I am jealous and desperate, when I see the happiness of the nations &c.
